Action Plan:
1. Arrange immediate emergency transfer: ambulance dispatched to patient’s home for urgent conveyance to nearest Emergency Department for stroke pathway activation and neuro-imaging (CT brain ± CTA) with consideration of IV thrombolysis / thrombectomy.
2. Safety instructions: patient advised to unlock front door, sit in hallway for rapid paramedic access; clinician to stay on the telephone until crew arrival.
3. Hospital to receive hand-over including history of sudden left arm paralysis, facial tingling, dysphagia, dysarthria, onset ≈1 hour prior to call, and vascular risk factors (type 2 diabetes, hypertension, ex-smoker, moderate alcohol use).
4. Current regular medicines (metformin, losartan, amlodipine) and penicillin allergy documented for hospital reconciliation.
5. Follow-up: stroke team will assume ongoing care; GP to review after hospital discharge.
6. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Reason for call: woke ~1 hour prior unable to move left arm; no pain.  
• Associated symptoms: left facial tingling; difficulty swallowing liquids; slowed/slurred speech. No left leg involvement. No facial asymmetry observed by patient.  
• Past medical history: type 2 diabetes; hypertension.  
• Medications: Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented); Losartan (dose/route/frequency not documented); Amlodipine (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Allergies: Penicillin → reported allergy (reaction details not provided).  
• Family history: Father – heart disease (details unknown).  
• Social history: Lives alone; ex-smoker; drinks “a few pints” of beer on weekends and a couple during the week.

Objective:
(Telephone consultation – no direct examination possible)  
• Patient-reported findings: complete motor loss in left arm; normal sensation in arm; left facial tingling; speech effortful/slowed; difficulty swallowing liquids.  
• No discoloration or coldness of left hand reported.  
• No left leg symptoms.  
• Vitals: not obtained.

Investigations: none performed pre-hospital.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Sudden left arm paralysis with facial sensory change and dysphasia
   - Assessment: Suspected acute ischemic cerebrovascular accident (stroke).
   - Differential: Intracerebral hemorrhage, Todd’s paresis, complex migraine (less likely).
   - Investigations planned: ED stroke protocol imaging (urgent non-contrast CT brain ± vascular imaging), ECG, labs (FBC, U&Es, coagulation profile, glucose, lipids).
   - Treatment planned: Pre-hospital care; rapid ED assessment; consider IV alteplase and/or mechanical thrombectomy per stroke team; secondary prevention thereafter.
   - Referrals: Emergency Department; on-call stroke team.

2. Type 2 diabetes mellitus
   - Assessment: Known T2DM, status pending hospital review.
   - Treatment planned: Continue metformin unless contraindicated by hospital team; monitor BGLs in hospital.

3. Hypertension
   - Assessment: Known hypertension, likely contributor to cerebrovascular risk.
   - Treatment planned: Continue losartan and amlodipine unless modified by stroke/medical team; BP monitoring in hospital.
